description:
Parent: fz-bfh. Regression target for the unified root fz-f98.

## Symptom, minimized

    fn main() do
      map = %{2 => :two, 1 => :one}
      dbg(Enum.reduce(map, fn ({k, _v}, {ak, av}) -> {ak + k, av} end))
    end

    fz      => fz panic: "Enum.EmptyError"
    elixir  => {3, :one}

`Enum.reduce/2` takes no accumulator, so it must seed from the FIRST element and
fold the rest. `Enum.EmptyError` is what Elixir raises for reduce/2 over an
EMPTY enumerable, so the shape of the defect is that the Map's first element
never reaches the seed path -- the enumerable is being treated as empty.

## Half of this ticket is already fixed

It originally covered reduce/2 AND reduce/3, and reported both as
"native attempted to materialize absent value ... native.rs:2826". Verified at
main 417c5b0b5:

    Enum.reduce(map, 0, fn ({k, _v}, acc) -> acc + k end)   => 3     CORRECT
    Enum.reduce(map, fn ({k, _v}, {ak, av}) -> ... end)     => raises

reduce/3 works on interp and run. The native materialization panic is gone
entirely -- do NOT start at native.rs:2826, the symptom moved layers.

## Why this is worth doing next

It is the ONLY thing standing between two deferred fixtures and green:

- `fz_f98_map_reduce` -- skipping only the reduce/2 line makes the fixture pass.
- `enum_tier0` -- this is the FIRST of its two blockers; with that one line
  skipped it prints eight further correct values before hitting fz-k22.

Both fixtures were re-triaged at main 417c5b0b5 and their headers name these
blockers exactly.

## Checks

- The three-line repro above returns `{3, :one}` on interp, run and build.
- `fz_f98_map_reduce` comes off deferral and is green on all three paths.
- `map_enumerable` stays green.
- Full lib + matrix at baseline or better.
title: Enum.reduce/2 over a Map raises Enum.EmptyError on a non-empty map
